belief: My value depends on how much I earn.
origins: When salary becomes the scoreboard, a raise feels like approval and a pay cut feels like a demotion of the self. This can come from families who compared incomes, workplaces that publicly ranked pay, or a culture that treats earnings as a measure of success. It can also arise from real need: when money is tight, earning more can feel like the only path to safety, and we slip from “I need more” to “I am worth more.”
teaches: Scripture says that we were redeemed not with perishable things such as silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ. The price of our worth has already been paid in the highest currency there is. The psalmist marvels that God is mindful of us and cares for us. We are told that we are worth more than many sparrows. A paycheck pays for work. It does not tell us who we are.
self_statements: The more I earn, the more I matter.
If someone earns more than me, they are worth more.
My salary is my report card.
I have to keep climbing to be worth anything.
People respect me for my income.
errors: Measuring my value against other people’s pay.
Treating a number as my identity.
Believing that I am either a high earner and successful or low and a failure.
Feeling small when the number is small and concluding that I am small.
questions: What would I say to a friend who believed this?
What did God pay for me, and what does that say about my value?
Whose pay do I compare mine to, and why?
What do I need to earn for security, and what part is about status?
What things do I contribute that no salary measures?
What would change if my worth were already settled?
truth: My salary measures the market’s price for a task, not God’s price for me. I was redeemed with the precious blood of Christ. I can pursue fair pay and wise provision without making the number my worth.
hw_truths: My worth was paid for by Christ.
My salary is not my value.
I can seek fair pay without needing it for identity.
I contribute in ways no paycheck measures.
I am loved at every income level.
log: Each week, write your biggest money thought and a sentence that separates the number from your worth.
actions: On one side list what you need to earn for security. On the other list what you feel you need for status.
Avoid checking what others earn this week and notice how you feel.
List five things you give that no one pays you for.
prayer: Lord, You paid a price for me that no salary could match. Free me from measuring myself by income. Help me work well, provide wisely, and rest in the value You have given me. Amen.
hw_questions: Whose income do I compare mine to?
What do I need versus what do I want for status?
What did Christ pay for me?
What do I give that is not paid?
What would change if my worth were settled?
What would I say to a friend?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Christ paid for me, so my worth is not set by my salary.”
